title: Sonntagessen
desc: Half past eleven to five, and the good plates
setting: A house in Kriens from 1974, six pairs of shoes at the door, and a woman with wet hands.

options.feedback: Five minutes early is right and fifteen is a little much. Naming it yourself takes it off her.
Frau Odermatt, and Sie, and wait to be told otherwise. That may take a year.
Her first name, on the first Sunday, unasked. Here that is the one move you do not make.

steps.speaker: Marianne
steps.es: Sie sind also aus dem Süden.
steps.en: So you are from the south.

options.es: Ja. Aus einer kleinen Stadt am Meer.
options.en: Yes. From a small town by the sea.
options.feedback: One more sentence than the question needed. That is the opening move and she will take it.
Correct and closed. She has thirty-nine more questions and now they all have to be hers.
Selina told her, three weeks ago, in detail. Everybody at this table knows more than they say.

steps.speaker: Kurt
steps.es: Wie ist das Wasser bei Ihnen?
steps.en: What is the water like where you come from?

options.es: Man kann es trinken. Es schmeckt nach nichts.
options.en: You can drink it. It tastes of nothing.
options.feedback: He is asking whether you can drink from the tap. It is his first question about any country.
Fair. He will not rephrase it, he will wait, and you will work it out in the silence.
He has asked you two questions in three hours. This is one of them.

options.es: Das ist eine gute Frage. Da muss ich noch schauen.
options.en: That is a good question. I still have to look into that.
options.feedback: The polite deflection, twice over. Nobody asks again, and nobody is offended.
Pay is private here. The pension is not, and neither is rent. The line sits somewhere else.
Honest, and she will now explain all three pillars over the roast. Which is not the worst outcome.
